from.description: The address of the first child to list: a previous page's `next`.

node.description: The address of the node whose children to list, as a level gives it; the crates, and what lies outside every crate, without it.

children.description: The page's children, in the order of the level: crates, modules, directories, then files, each kind by its path.

address.description: Its address: `node` set to it lists the nodes it holds.

crate.description: Present on a child of kind `crate` alone.

dependencies.description: Its path and workspace dependencies, by the table of its manifest that states them, when its manifest is read.

endpoint.description: `crate`: a crate of the tree; `unwalked`: a path whose directory holds no walked manifest; `no_workspace_root`: a workspace dependency of a crate with no workspace root the walked manifests show; `not_in_workspace`: a workspace dependency its root does not name.

value.description: For `crate` the crate's address, a child of the top level; for `unwalked` the path as the manifest writes it; for the other two the dependency's name.

endpoint.description: `crate`: a crate of the tree; `unwalked`: a path whose directory holds no walked manifest; `no_workspace_root`: a workspace dependency of a crate with no workspace root the walked manifests show; `not_in_workspace`: a workspace dependency its root does not name.

value.description: For `crate` the crate's address, a child of the top level; for `unwalked` the path as the manifest writes it; for the other two the dependency's name.

endpoint.description: `crate`: a crate of the tree; `unwalked`: a path whose directory holds no walked manifest; `no_workspace_root`: a workspace dependency of a crate with no workspace root the walked manifests show; `not_in_workspace`: a workspace dependency its root does not name.

value.description: For `crate` the crate's address, a child of the top level; for `unwalked` the path as the manifest writes it; for the other two the dependency's name.

omitted.description: The dependencies the page left out of the tables, every one, when the crate passes a page with them.

manifest.description: `read`, or `unread` when its manifest has no index (a syntax error, a file past its size), so its package and dependencies are unknown.

package.description: Its package name, when its manifest is read and names one.

decisions.description: The decisions anchored in it, each once: one of whose anchors names a walked file at or below it, or a directory whose walked files all are.

definitions.description: The definitions the index holds of the walked files at or below it.

non_test.description: The definitions neither marked test code nor in a file that is.

unindexed_files.description: The files with no index (unread, not UTF-8, too large or too complex to index), whose definitions both counts leave out.

file.description: Present on a child of kind `file` alone.

doc.description: The first paragraph of its doc the index holds: a Rust file's.

cut.description: Whether the paragraph runs on past `text`, the bytes of it the index holds.

imports.description: The Rust imports of the files below it that resolve to a file: those into the other children of the level, listed, and the dependency imports into files outside the level, counted.

omitted.description: The edges the page left out of `siblings`, every one, when the child passes a page with them.

outside_level.description: The dependency imports into files outside the level, counted and not listed; re-exports are left out.

siblings.description: Into the files below the other children of the level, by the order of the child they go to.

count.description: The dependency imports: every import but a re-export. 0 for an edge of re-exports alone, which is listed.

reexports.description: The re-exports: `use`s a visibility opens, which are no dependency.

test_only.description: Whether every one of them, dependency or re-export, is test code.

to.description: The address of the child they go to.

place.description: `in_module`: a Rust file at its module; `no_module`: a file of a language with no modules, or a manifest; `unreached`: a Rust file no target's mod declarations reach; `unresolved_several`: one reached at two or more module paths; `unresolved_in_item`: one a mod inside a function or another item declares; `unresolved_two_files`: one declared where both name.rs and name/mod.rs are.

kind.description: `crate`, with the key `crate`; `outside_crates`: what lies outside every crate, from the code root, first of the top level when it is there; `module`: a Rust module, its own file or files and the modules below it, with the key `module`; `directory`: files in no Rust module; `file`, with the key `file`.

lines.description: The lines of the walked files at or below it.

counted.description: The lines of the files whose bytes were read.

unread_files.description: The files none of whose bytes were read (past the size a source file may have, unreadable), whose lines `counted` leaves out.

module.description: Present on a child of kind `module` alone.

doc.description: The first paragraph of its own file's doc the index holds, when it has one own file and no other.

cut.description: Whether the paragraph runs on past `text`, the bytes of it the index holds.

imports.description: The Rust imports of the files below it that resolve to a file: those into the other children of the level, listed, and the dependency imports into files outside the level, counted.

omitted.description: The edges the page left out of `siblings`, every one, when the child passes a page with them.

outside_level.description: The dependency imports into files outside the level, counted and not listed; re-exports are left out.

siblings.description: Into the files below the other children of the level, by the order of the child they go to.

count.description: The dependency imports: every import but a re-export. 0 for an edge of re-exports alone, which is listed.

reexports.description: The re-exports: `use`s a visibility opens, which are no dependency.

test_only.description: Whether every one of them, dependency or re-export, is test code.

to.description: The address of the child they go to.

name.description: The last segment of its path: of a crate's or a root module's directory, `.` for the code root, a module's own name, a directory's or a file's; `outside_crates` for what lies outside every crate.

unresolved_imports.description: The Rust imports of the files at or below it that resolve to no file, re-exports included.

decisions.description: The decisions anchored in the node whose level this is, each once; at the top, every decision of the graph.

decisions_in_no_child.description: Those of `decisions` anchored in no one child: through a directory whose walked files lie under two children or more, and at the top through no walked file.

next.description: The address of the first child after the page: `from` lists from it.

omitted.description: The children after the page, when it leaves any out.

too_large.description: The children between the page's first and `next` that no page lists: one whose record passes a page of its own even with its list left out, or whose address takes more than a quarter of the result.

total.description: The children of the level, on every page.

truncated.description: Present only when the result was cut to fit the result budget: each cut, by JSON pointer, with what it omitted.

file.description: The address of a file, as a level gives it: `file:<path>`.

from_position.description: The position of the first item to list: a previous page's `next`.

address.description: Its address, as a level gives it.

cause.description: Present when it is not `indexed`: why, as a sentence.

definitions.description: Its definitions, in the order of their spans in the file.

doc.description: The first paragraph of its doc the index holds: a Rust definition's.

cut.description: Whether the paragraph runs on past `text`, the bytes of it the index holds.

first_line.description: The first line of its span, its attributes and doc comments included.

impls.description: Present on a struct, an enum or a union of a Rust file alone.

elsewhere.description: Present when `types_named` is 1: the impls of the name in the other walked Rust files, by file, then by line. Every inherent impl of the name, however written, and a trait impl whose self type has no path before the name (`T`, `&T`, `T<U>`, `dyn T`); one written `std::io::Error` or `crate::x::T` is not listed. Matched by the name alone: a generic parameter or a type a `use` renames to it is taken for it, an impl through a type alias of another name is not found, and an inherent impl with no member is not listed.

first_line.description: A trait impl's first line; an inherent impl's first member's, as the index holds its members alone.

last_line.description: Its last line; an inherent impl's last member's.

path.description: Its path's segments, outermost first: those of what holds it, the type's name, then a trait impl's `<Trait>`.

omitted.description: The impls the page left out of `elsewhere`, every one, when the definition passes a page with them.

types_named.description: The structs, enums, unions, traits and type aliases of the walked Rust files that have this type's name, this one included.

last_line.description: The last line of its span.

path.description: Its path's segments as the index spells them, outermost first, as an anchor's symbol joins them with `::`: a definition is nested in the one whose path its own extends.

test.description: Whether it is test code, by its own mark or its file's.

visibility.description: Who may name it, where its source states it.

doc.description: The first paragraph of its doc the index holds: a Rust file's.

cut.description: Whether the paragraph runs on past `text`, the bytes of it the index holds.

index_state.description: `indexed`, or why the index holds none of it, so it lists no definition: `too_large` (past the size a source file may have, or its kind is indexed within), `not_a_file`, `unreadable`, `no_thread` (no thread to index it on started), `not_utf8`, `syntax` (TOML or JSON that does not parse), `too_complex` (past its budget of work or size), `too_deep` (a path past the nesting bound), `grammar` (a grammar the parser does not load), `too_many_indentations` (a Python file).

line_count.description: Its line count; absent when its bytes were not read, which `index_state` says why.

name.description: Its file name, the last segment of its path.

next.description: The position of the first item after the page: `from_position` lists from it.

omitted.description: The items after the page, when it leaves any out.

on_file.description: The decisions with an anchor on the file whole, or on a directory above it, with no symbol: they cover every line, and no range lists them, whatever their symbol anchors cover. By name.

ranges.description: Its lines cut into ranges, from line 1 to its line count with no gap or overlap, each covered by one set of the decisions not in `on_file`, through the spans their symbol anchors resolve to; a range ends where that set changes. None when its bytes were not read or it has no line.

decisions.description: The decisions one of whose symbol anchors resolves to a span covering each of its lines, by name; empty where none does.

too_large.description: The items between the page's first and `next` that no page lists, as one passes a page alone even with its impls left out.

total.description: The items of the frame, on every page: the four lists below, over all pages.

truncated.description: Present only when the result was cut to fit the result budget: each cut, by JSON pointer, with what it omitted.

unspanned_anchors.description: The symbol anchors on the file that resolve to no definition in this tree, so they cover no line, with their finding. By decision.

cause.description: What makes it one, as a sentence.

kind.description: Its finding, as `status` names it with git not asked: `unresolved`: the file defines nothing its symbol names, on a decision ever accepted; `planned`: the same on a decision never accepted, as `trurlic check` names it; `malformed`: a symbol out of the grammar; `ambiguous`: its symbol names definitions of several paths, none of which it covers; `unverified`: the file has no index.

from_position.description: The position of the first hit to list: a previous page's `next`.

query.description: The text to find, ASCII letters of either case alike: 1 to 256 bytes of UTF-8, which the lengths here count in characters and so state exactly for ASCII alone, and no control character (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F).

hits.description: The page's hits, in rank: by `match`, the better first, then the shorter path, then the path's bytes; then a node before a definition, nodes by address, definitions by file, lines and kind.

address.description: Present on a node's hit alone: its address, `node` of a level.

definition.description: Present on a hit of kind `definition` alone.

file.description: Its file's address, `file` of a frame.

first_line.description: The first line of its span: where its file's frame shows it.

last_line.description: The last line of its span.

path.description: Its path's segments as the index spells them, outermost first.

kind.description: A node's kind, as a level names it, or `definition`, with the key `definition`.

match.description: `exact_name`: its name is the query; `name_prefix`: its name starts with it; `path_substring`: its path holds it. A node's path is a crate's, a directory's or a file's, a root module's root directory, any other module's segments joined by `::`, none for what lies outside every crate; a definition's is its segments joined by `::`.

name.description: A node's name as a level gives it: the last segment of its path, `.` for the code root's crate, `outside_crates` for what lies outside every crate. A definition's last segment.

next.description: The position of the first hit after the page: `from_position` lists from it.

omitted.description: The hits after the page, when it leaves any out.

too_large.description: The hits between the page's first and `next` that no page lists, as one passes a page alone.

total.description: Every hit of the query, on every page.

truncated.description: Present only when the result was cut to fit the result budget: each cut, by JSON pointer, with what it omitted.
